confirmed.title: Cover is the last thing in a 354 KB body, so the page paints before the cover exists
confirmed.detail: The brief says the cover is 'shown before first paint', but html[data-intro="on"] only gates a rule; the element that rule displays is rendered after <Nav />, {children}, <Footer />, <MotionToggle /> and <TransitionLayer />. In the built page (.next/server/app/index.html, 354,465 bytes) `<header` is at byte 4,323, `id="hero-heading"` at 9,976 and `class="intro fixed` at 326,377. Browsers render incrementally as bytes arrive, so on anything but an instant connection the visitor sees the nav, the hero copy (which has no Reveal) and the before-drawing painted first, then the black cover snaps on over them and the mark starts growing. A second consequence: markRemaining() (Intro.tsx:41) assumes the .intro-mark CSS entrance began at first-contentful-paint, but the entrance begins when the layer's markup is finally parsed, so slide() fires while the mark is still scaling in; the same happens for a background tab, where Chrome has no FCP entry yet when visibilitychange fires (paint = 0, so the slide starts 40 ms after the tab is shown). Fix: render <Intro /> as the first child of <body>, directly after the boot <script> (it is position: fixed and z-[100], so document order costs nothing; useLenis works anywhere), and time the slide from the mark's own animationend with the timer only as a fallback, or from the layer's own paint rather than FCP.

confirmed.title: Lenis stop/start reflows the viewport width, so the centred lockup jumps on classic-scrollbar desktops
confirmed.detail: lenis.stop() sets isStopped, which adds the lenis-stopped class (lenis.mjs updateClassName), and globals.css:110 turns that into `overflow: clip` on html; on the root, clip propagates to the viewport as hidden, so the scrollbar disappears. On Windows and Linux desktops (the only visitors who get Lenis: fine pointer, non-static tier) the fixed .intro layer therefore widens by the scrollbar width (~17 px) when the [lenis] effect at line 65 calls stop() right after hydration, and the lockup at `left: 50%` jumps ~8 px right while the mark is growing in; at handoff() line 144 start() narrows it again and the 2.4x lockup jumps ~8 px left in the same frame the FLIP begins (GSAP's cached x/y are relative to the layout position, which moved). The comment on lines 141-142 says the reflow happens under the opaque cover, but the lockup is on top of the cover. Fix: either drop lenis.stop()/start() from the intro entirely (the layer already swallows wheel, touchmove and scroll keys with stopPropagation, so Lenis never receives input while the cover is up), or set `scrollbar-gutter: stable` on html so the gutter survives overflow: clip.

votes.reason:
Reproducible from the code as it stands; I could not refute any link in the chain.

1. Scrollbar present at first paint. The boot script (src/app/layout.tsx:48) sets html[data-intro="on"]; globals.css uses that attribute only for `.intro` display (369) and `[data-logo]` visibility (376). Nothing hides the scrollbar, every page is taller than the viewport, so on a classic-scrollbar desktop the vertical scrollbar exists from first paint. The `.intro` layer is `fixed inset-0` (Intro.tsx:222), so its width is the layout viewport minus the scrollbar, and `.intro-lockup` sits at `left: 50%` of it (globals.css:383-388).

2. stop() fires right after hydration, with the mark visible. Intro is the last child inside SmoothScroll (layout.tsx:51-59), so Intro's mount effect runs first: `locked.current = true`, `lenisRef.current` is still null (Intro.tsx:91-92). SmoothScroll's effect then runs `detectTier()` (src/lib/capabilities.ts:34-45): a Windows/Linux desktop with WebGL and a fine pointer is "lite"/"full", `coarse` is false, so Lenis is constructed (SmoothScroll.tsx:55-71) with the default `autoToggle = false` (lenis.mjs:434) and published. Intro's `useLenis()` re-renders it and the `[lenis]` effect at Intro.tsx:65 calls `lenis.stop()` -> `internalStop()` -> `isStopped = true` -> `updateClassName()` (lenis.mjs:703-716, 1002-1006, 1044-1048), which adds `lenis-stopped` to `document.documentElement` (rootElement for wrapper=window, lenis.mjs:946). globals.css:110 `.lenis.lenis-stopped { overflow: clip }` then applies to html; html's overflow is no longer `visible`, so its value (not body's) propagates to the viewport, where clip is treated as hidden (CSS Overflow 3; Lenis's own shipped lenis.css uses exactly this rule to kill native scroll). The scrollbar goes, the layout viewport widens by the scrollbar width, the `.intro` layer widens, and the lockup's `left: 50%` anchor moves right by half the scrollbar width. The mark is a sibling painted above the cover, positioned by that anchor, so it visibly shifts while (or just after) its 500 ms CSS entrance plays.

3. start() at handoff reverses it in the FLIP's first frame. Intro.tsx:144 `start()` -> `internalStart()` -> `isStopped = false` -> class removed -> html back to `overflow: visible` -> body's `overflow-x: clip` / `overflow-y: visible` propagate -> vertical auto -> scrollbar returns -> viewport narrows. `centre()` at line 146 forces layout and reads the narrowed layer, so the target maths is correct, but the tween starts from the x/y `slide()` set (line 185), which are translate offsets on an anchor that has just moved left; the next painted frame shows the 2.4x lockup half a scrollbar to the left of where it was, then the FLIP runs smoothly from there. The comment at 141-142 is true for the page under the opaque cover but not for the lockup above it.

Population: Windows 10 in any browser, Chrome/Edge on Windows 11 with default classic scrollbars, Linux without overlay scrollbars, macOS with "Show scroll bars: Always". macOS overlay scrollbars have no width, so it never shows on the owner's machine. `.lenis.lenis-stopped { overflow: clip }` exists at HEAD; what is new in this tree is calling stop()/start() while a viewport-centred element is on screen. No `scrollbar-gutter` anywhere in src, docs or README. Severity minor: two shifts of roughly half the scrollbar width (about 7-9 px) inside a ~1.5 s sequence.
votes.fix:
Smallest correct fix: reserve the gutter so the stopped state does not change the viewport width. In src/app/globals.css, on the existing `html { ... }` block (line 95), add `scrollbar-gutter: stable;`. With the gutter reserved, `overflow: clip` on html (treated as hidden on the viewport) keeps the same width, so the `.intro` layer and the lockup's `left: 50%` anchor never move on stop() or start(); every page on the site is taller than the viewport, so the reserved gutter changes nothing visually elsewhere, and it removes the same hidden reflow around the pre-existing `lenis?.stop()` / `lenis?.start()` calls in src/components/motion/Transition.tsx (lines 52, 88, 141, 157) for free. Then reword the comment at src/components/chrome/Intro.tsx:141-142 (it currently claims the reflow is invisible under the cover): e.g. "Scrolling comes back before the measure; html reserves its scrollbar gutter (globals.css), so the layer's width, and the lockup's centre, do not move when the scrollbar returns."

Alternative (larger): drop the four Lenis calls and the `[lenis]` effect / `locked` ref from Intro.tsx entirely, since the layer already swallows wheel, touchmove and scroll keys. Trade-off: on classic-scrollbar desktops the scrollbar track sits outside the cover's hit area, so a visitor could drag it during the intro; the gutter fix keeps the lock and is one line, so prefer it.

confirmed.title: Comment claims the intro consults a remembered 'Pause motion', but Intro never reads paused and the attribute is not set yet when it looks
confirmed.detail: Intro.tsx does not subscribe to `paused` or read html[data-paused] anywhere; the GSAP slide, hold and FLIP play in full under a remembered pause. Even if it did look, MotionToggle's first effect calls setPaused(true) from sessionStorage, which only schedules a re-render, and its second effect writes data-paused in that later commit, so in the commit where Intro's effect runs (same flush, sibling order) data-paused is still absent. The only thing the pause affects is the CSS mark entrance (globals.css:400, `animation: none`), which is applied a commit late and cuts the mark to its end state a few ms in. Failure scenario: a visitor who pressed 'Pause motion' on a previous page of the visit reloads and still gets the full opening sequence (the site's own rule is that Pause motion stops what moves on its own). Fix: either have Intro read useExperience.getState().paused (and sessionStorage, since the store is not yet updated) and take the early-return path, or change the comment so nobody relies on an ordering that does nothing.

confirmed.title: Cover sits at the end of a 354 KB document, so first paint can be the bare page with no nav logo
confirmed.detail: What is wrong: the whole intro premise is 'cover in the server HTML, shown before first paint'. But <Intro /> is rendered last in <body> (after Footer, MotionToggle, TransitionLayer). In the prerendered .next/server/app/index.html the cover markup starts at byte 326,377 of 354,465; the boot script (byte 3,928), the nav [data-logo] (byte 4,858) and the hero heading (byte 9,976) are all at the top. Browsers render progressively while the HTML streams in: once the render-blocking CSS has arrived, Chrome/Safari paint whatever has been parsed so far. On any connection where the tail of the document has not arrived by then (3G/4G, a cold edge, a slow TTFB with streaming), the first frame is the nav plus the hero, and because the boot script already set html[data-intro="on"], the nav's [data-logo] is visibility:hidden in that frame: the visitor sees the page with a missing logo, then the cover pops in over it, then the logo sequence. This is the opposite of the intended 'never a blank or unmasked frame', and it also makes markRemaining() (which keys off first-contentful-paint) time the slide off the flash rather than the cover. Fix: render <Intro /> as the first element in <body>, right after the boot script (it is position:fixed z-100, so DOM order changes nothing visually). useLenis reads a module-level store, not React context, and Intro never reads `paused`, so it does not need to be inside <SmoothScroll> or after <MotionToggle>; the comment on line 57 claiming the MotionToggle ordering matters is inaccurate.

confirmed.title: Keyboard focus is not contained under the cover: Tab lands on invisible controls and Enter acts on them
confirmed.detail: What is wrong: blockKeys swallows only SCROLL_KEYS. Tab is not swallowed and nothing behind the cover is made inert, so the page stays fully tabbable while the z-100 cover is up.
